prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” broker for every self‑employed person in Kansas City — the right broker depends on your budget, whether you want Marketplace (ACA) coverage and subsidies, if you need help with HRAs/QSEHRA, your preferred carriers, and how much hand‑holding you want. That said, here’s a practical approach and some options to find a great broker for your situation.

How to choose the best broker for a self‑employed person
- Use an independent broker who represents multiple carriers (not captive to one insurer).  
- Confirm experience with self‑employed needs: ACA Marketplace enrollment, subsidy eligibility, QSEHRA/HRAs, small‑group vs. individual plan differences.  
- Ask how they’re paid and whether they will help with renewals, claims issues, and subsidy reconciliation. Most individual plan brokers are paid by carriers, but get it on record.  
- Check credentials/reviews: NAHU membership, state licensing via the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance, Google/Yelp reviews, and client references.  
- Get quotes from 2–3 brokers/agencies so you can compare plan options, networks, and total out‑of‑pocket costs.

Places to look right away
- Local independent agencies in Kansas City: search Google/Maps for “independent health insurance broker Kansas City MO” and review ratings. Local agencies are often better at network nuances.  
- National online brokers/comparison sites that serve self‑employed people: eHealth, Policygenius, HealthSherpa (good for Marketplace), and Stride (freelancers/gig workers). These can be fast and let you compare plans across carriers.  
- Healthcare.gov agents and assister organizations (if you plan to use the ACA Marketplace/subsidies). They can enroll you in Marketplace plans and help with subsidy questions.  
- Professional associations: NAHU’s “Find an Agent” tool or the Missouri Department of Insurance’s license lookup to verify a broker’s standing.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- How many self‑employed or individual clients do you work with? Can you give references?  
- Do you represent multiple carriers? Which ones commonly offered in KC?  
- Do you help with ACA subsidy calculations and annual renewals?  
- Can you explain QSEHRA or other small‑business tax‑advantaged options if I want to offer myself a benefit?  
- What are your fees or how are you compensated? Will you help with claims or appeals?  
- Do you assist with provider network checks and cost estimates for my regular doctors/prescriptions?

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated local brokers and agencies in Kansas City if you give me your ZIP code; or  
- Compare a few quoted plans if you tell me age(s), household income (for subsidy eligibility), and whether you prefer Marketplace plans.

Which route do you prefer — I can find local broker names and contact info for your ZIP code, or run through plan types and trade‑offs now.
